componentDescription.client: Where requests come from: the people using your system.
componentDescription.lb: Spreads incoming requests across the servers behind it so no single one is swamped.
componentDescription.web-server: Runs your application code and answers HTTP requests. Add CPUs or copies to serve more.
componentDescription.postgres: A relational database that keeps data safe. Read replicas share the reading load.
componentDescription.mobile: People on phones, sending requests over mobile networks.
componentDescription.dns: Turns a domain name into an address so people can reach your system.
componentDescription.cdn: Keeps copies of static content close to people so it loads faster.
componentDescription.api-gateway: One front door: checks who is calling, routes and combines the APIs behind it.
componentDescription.rate-limiter: Turns away requests when one caller sends too many too quickly.
componentDescription.worker: Does slow jobs in the background, taking work from a queue.
componentDescription.scheduler: Runs jobs at set times, such as a report every night.
componentDescription.read-replica: A read-only copy of the database that takes some of the reading load.
componentDescription.kv-store: Stores data by key; very fast reads and writes, easy to split up.
componentDescription.search: Finds text by keyword across a large amount of content.
componentDescription.redis: An in-memory cache that takes reads off the database.
componentDescription.memcached: A simple in-memory cache spread across several machines.
componentDescription.queue: Holds work to be done later so people do not wait for it.
componentDescription.rabbitmq: A message queue with routing and delivery receipts.
componentDescription.stream: A durable log of events that many readers can replay.
componentDescription.object-storage: Stores big files such as photos and video, cheaply and almost without limit.
componentDescription.third-party: Someone else’s service your system calls, such as payments.
